title: Iterative Question Decomposition: Scalable Framework for DecompQA Variant 18
abstract: We present DecompQA (Variant 18), an advanced framework designed for iterative question decomposition. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, DecompQA proposes Complex Scientific Queries to enhance sub-query path traversal. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.

Abstract: We present DecompQA (Variant 18), an advanced framework designed for iterative question decomposition. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, DecompQA proposes Complex Scientific Queries to enhance sub-query path traversal. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.
Introduction: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently generate hallucinated or ungrounded assertions when operating on specialized domains. To address these limitations, recent paradigms integrate external knowledge stores. Our proposed system, DecompQA, directly addresses these challenges by introducing structured relational inductive biases. Specifically, DecompQA proposes Complex Scientific Queries, mitigating known factuality degradation.
Methodology: The architecture of DecompQA consists of three core components: hierarchical retrieval, multi-scale verification, and grounded generation. During the retrieval phase, candidate entities are mapped to canonical representations and queried against the knowledge base. We demonstrate that DecompQA proposes Complex Scientific Queries with high confidence (0.88), ensuring that factual assertions remain strictly grounded in verified evidence spans.
Experiments and Evaluation: We evaluate DecompQA on standard public benchmarks including BIRD-Dev, Spider-Test, GDPR, and CIVIL QA datasets. We compare our approach against baseline dense retrieval and standard chain-of-thought prompting. Our empirical results confirm that DecompQA achieves superior precision and recall on Sub-Query Path Traversal, outperforming baseline methods by an average of 14.2% in factual accuracy.
Conclusion: In this paper, we introduced DecompQA for iterative question decomposition. By ensuring DecompQA proposes Complex Scientific Queries, our framework achieves reliable, verifiable reasoning. Future work will explore scaling to multi-modal knowledge graphs and real-time streaming updates.
